themes.name: Receipts vanish without warning
themes.insight: All 3 of 3 participants lose receipts silently when signal drops, with no error or retry, so they only learn from finance or end-of-week reports and fall back to paper, email or texted photos.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: So someone buys props or lunch for the crew, they take a picture of the receipt in the app, it looks like it worked, and then the next day it's just not there.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: In the first month? I counted at least nine missing receipts from shoot days alone.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: If people don't believe the photo went through, they go back to emailing me, and then I've got two systems.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: I ended up telling the producers to keep the paper in an envelope until they see it show up on their list.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: And make the receipt thing tell you if it didn't actually send. Even a little red dot. Anything.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: Because I get the "missing receipt" report at the end of the week and it's like twenty lines long.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: Half the time the photo's not in the app anymore.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: And make the photo thing keep the picture until it's actually sent. Don't make them start over.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: A few just text me photos of receipts now. Which, fine, I forward them in, but that's me doing data entry at night.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: Meaning it never made it to me. There's no draft, there's no error

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: But a lot of our stops are out past where there's any signal.

quotes.speaker: Hannah Cho
quotes.text: I'll attach a receipt and it'll start sending and then the signal drops and — it doesn't seem to come back.

quotes.speaker: Hannah Cho
quotes.text: Finance flagged them. I had four expenses kicked back last month because of "missing receipt," and I know I'd attached them.

quotes.speaker: Hannah Cho
quotes.text: Things just quietly don't go through.

quotes.speaker: Hannah Cho
quotes.text: And if a receipt doesn't send, keep trying, or at least tell me. Don't make me find out from finance.

themes.name: Approval chain too rigid
themes.insight: Anecdote (1 voice, Dana): the fixed approval chain suits large firms, not a 48-person studio, so small purchases stall and admins invent placeholder approvers.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: When we set it up, the approval flow wants a chain. Submitter, then their manager, then a department head, then finance.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: Lena made a placeholder user called "Studio Approvals" so the chain would save.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: A nine-dollar parking ticket goes through the exact same three steps as a two-thousand-dollar equipment rental.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: You can rename the steps, you can add steps, but you can't really take them away below a certain point.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: Let me turn off steps for small amounts.

themes.name: Xero export needs manual fixing
themes.insight: Anecdote (1 voice, Dana): the Xero export drops client tracking and miscodes categories while the mapping screen looks correct, costing about two evenings of manual rework.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: In practice, the first month I had to redo, I want to say, a third of the coded lines.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: And our tracking categories — we track by client — those just didn't come through at all. Every line showed up with no client attached.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: But the mapping screen says everything is mapped correctly. That's the confusing part. It looks right and the result is wrong.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: Two evenings, roughly. We had to export to a spreadsheet, fix the codes, and re-import into Xero by hand.

themes.name: Card limits are unclear
themes.insight: Anecdote (1 voice, Marcus): layered card limits and a rolling reset show only one number, causing 6–7 declines in three weeks and reimbursements through the old process.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: Declines? I'd say six or seven in three weeks.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: I thought the limit reset on the first of the month. It doesn't.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: One number. Show me one number that's the real amount they can spend right now.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: He paid with his own card and I reimbursed him through the old way. Which, again, is the thing we were trying to get rid of.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: And the screen only shows one number. So I'm looking at four hundred and he's standing at a pump in the middle of nowhere with a truck that's empty.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: There's the monthly limit, and then there's a per-transaction limit

themes.name: Mobile app unusable in the field
themes.insight: The mobile app fails the people who need it most in the field: gloved drivers face tiny buttons and surprise logouts, and a blind consultant can't use the unlabelled receipt button, so both work around the main flow.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: The app? For my guys it's unusable. I'm sorry, but it is.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: The buttons are tiny. These guys are wearing work gloves half the day.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: And it logs them out. Not every day, but like every few days they open it and it wants a password.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: Too many screens to get to one thing. I gave up on it after a couple of days.

quotes.speaker: Hannah Cho
quotes.text: But the button to take a picture of a receipt — the screen reader just says "button." That's it. No label.

quotes.speaker: Hannah Cho
quotes.text: And on the camera screen itself, the shutter doesn't say anything at all.

quotes.speaker: Hannah Cho
quotes.text: It's maybe six extra steps. But it means I'm doing receipts at night in the hotel instead of right there.

quotes.speaker: Hannah Cho
quotes.text: I got a nice reply saying they'd pass it on. That was three weeks ago.

quotes.speaker: Hannah Cho
quotes.text: It's frustrating because it's literally one label. It's the one button the whole app is built around and it's the one I can't use.

quotes.speaker: Hannah Cho
quotes.text: That part's okay. The fields are labeled, so VoiceOver reads them out, and I can pick the client from a list.

quotes.speaker: Hannah Cho
quotes.text: Honestly, really well, by accident. It was just email, and email I can do in my sleep.

themes.name: Cards and reporting land well
themes.insight: Two participants (Dana, Marcus) name something that works: own cards for staff and spend reporting, which gives teams a reason to stay.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: The cards themselves. People like having their own card instead of borrowing mine.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: The reporting on the website is nice. I can see spend by truck, which I've never been able to do.
